tasks.short: Prepare agendas, capture meeting discussions, and produce approved minutes.

steps.what: Collect agenda items and supporting papers through the {EMAIL}.
Arrange agenda items and paper links in the {DOCS}.
Approve agenda priorities and timing.
Attend the meeting and capture decisions, actions, and important qualifications.
Turn meeting notes into structured minutes in the {DOCS}.

loop.input: Meeting notes, approved agenda, and minutes template; authorised audio only when available.
loop.output: Draft minutes and action list with source references and unresolved ambiguities.
loop.check: Validate names, dates, and required fields; link decisions to notes; flag unsupported owners or deadlines.
loop.stop: One draft and one repair pass per meeting; unresolved passages return to the clerk.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates arrange fields but cannot reliably interpret discussion notes and distinguish proposals from decisions.

steps.what: Resolve disputed wording and approve minutes and action ownership.
Distribute approved minutes through the {EMAIL} and record actions in the {PROJECT}.

tasks.design: A configured {WORKFLOW} collects agenda submissions and fills templates in the {DOCS}. A bounded model drafts minutes from meeting notes, with optional authorised transcription; chair approval releases minutes through the {EMAIL} and actions into the {PROJECT}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Agenda collection was fragmented, and interpreting discussion notes required substantial editing. Recording also raised access and retention questions.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing forms, templates, and approval flows cover coordination. Bounded drafting can reduce transcription and formatting work without deciding what the meeting agreed.
tasks.still_hard: Disputed decisions, unclear speakers, confidential discussions, and implied commitments need human interpretation. Meeting attendance remains a substantial part of the task.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise disagreement, preserve qualifications, and establish whether someone actually accepted an action.

ambition.what: Weekly overdue-decision briefing for the meeting chair.

tasks.altitude: The clerk spends less time assembling papers and more time clarifying decisions and following unresolved actions. Approval rights remain with the meeting chair.

reach.learn: Distinguish actions, decisions, dependencies, and escalation thresholds.

evidence.claim: Amberscript provides machine transcription and human-checked transcription; this supports transcription availability, not automatic minute accuracy.
Published research documents invented speech in transcription outputs, supporting source checks before approving minutes.
Agenda assembly, approval routing, and action creation can use templates and deterministic workflows; effort ranges are pilot estimates.

assumptions: The task concerns ordinary internal meetings, with concise minutes rather than mandatory verbatim records.
Time shares include chair approval effort and reflect substantial attendance time.
Estimates cover one meeting format and existing systems.
GDPR applies to notes and recordings. Audio requires an established lawful basis, notice, controlled access, and retention.
EU AI Act obligations and consultation under national rules are assessed for the intended deployment.
unknowns: Whether recording is permitted and acceptable to participants.
Which meetings require formal or verbatim records.
Available connectors, approval functions, and document permissions.
Applicable national consultation requirements and local approval lead times.
research_questions: Does a pilot preserve decisions, dissent, action owners, and deadlines across representative meetings?
Can existing configuration assemble agendas and publish approved actions without custom integrations?
new_work: Review unsupported statements and ambiguous action ownership.
Maintain agenda templates, distribution permissions, and action mappings.
Apply recording and draft-retention rules where audio is used.

tasks.short: Teach colleagues office procedures and computer applications, then check practical understanding.

steps.what: Discuss the learner's tasks, current knowledge, and difficulties.
Prepare instructions, screenshots, and practice exercises in the {DOCS}.

loop.input: Approved office procedure, learning needs, verified screenshots, and training template.
loop.output: Draft training guide and practice exercise linked to the approved procedure.
loop.check: The clerk checks application steps in a test context, source coverage, accessibility, and absence of live personal data.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision per guide; unsupported steps return to manual preparation.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates handle layout; adapting explanations and realistic exercises to different learning needs requires language generation.

steps.what: Arrange the session and send materials through the {CALENDAR} and {EMAIL}.
Demonstrate the procedure and explain when to use it.
Observe learner practice, answer questions, and correct misunderstandings.
Record attendance and arrange follow-up in the {LMS}.

tasks.design: A bounded drafting tool turns approved procedures in the {DOCS} into reviewed guides and practice exercises. Configuration in the {CALENDAR} and {LMS} handles bookings, attendance, and follow-up while the clerk teaches and assesses practical understanding.
tasks.previous_blocker: Guides needed manual adaptation, and session administration sat apart from training records. Individual learning difficulties resisted standard scripts.
tasks.enabler_now: Bounded drafting reduces preparation effort, while existing scheduling and learning functions cover routine administration.
tasks.still_hard: Confidence, accessibility needs, tacit knowledge, and safe application of procedures require direct observation and patient coaching.
tasks.human_edge: Notice hesitation, explain a concept differently, and distinguish memorised clicks from practical understanding.

ambition.what: Asynchronous office-application refreshers for remote starters.

tasks.altitude: The clerk spends more preparation time tailoring practice and less time formatting guides or arranging sessions. They can adapt teaching within approved procedures; certification and access rights do not change.

reach.learn: Assess learning needs and use aggregate feedback without ranking individual employees.

evidence.claim: Scheduling, attendance records, and reminders commonly use configured learning and calendar functions.
Drafting can assist preparation, but practical teaching and assessment remain human; estimates require a local pilot.

assumptions: Training concerns ordinary office procedures rather than regulated professional certification.
A basic {LMS} is available; a configured {WORKFLOW} record can substitute if absent.
Most demonstration and coaching time remains human, consistent with the task's communication-heavy prior.
Estimates cover one application and a small set of approved procedures.
GDPR and EU AI Act requirements apply; employee consultation follows national rules where applicable.
unknowns: Available training records, test accounts, and approved procedures.
Learner languages, accessibility needs, and remote-working patterns.
Whether proposed learning analytics trigger consultation under national rules.
research_questions: Can learners complete a representative task after using the reviewed guide?
Which existing learning and scheduling functions remove administration without custom code?
new_work: Verify generated instructions against the current application.
Refresh screenshots and exercises after procedure changes.
Check attendance exceptions and accessibility feedback.

tasks.short: Count, weigh, measure, organise, and record office materials.

steps.what: Find the material list and handling instructions in the {DOCS}.
Identify materials and count items against the checklist.
Weigh and measure materials with {OTHER} scales and measuring tools.
Sort materials into labelled groups and storage locations.
Enter quantities, measurements, and locations into the shared {SPREADSHEET}.
Compare totals with requirements and recount discrepancies.

tasks.design: Configure a material checklist from the {DOCS} and validated entry forms over the existing {SPREADSHEET}. Formulas calculate totals, convert units, and flag discrepancies; the clerk still counts, measures, and handles materials.
tasks.previous_blocker: Most work is physical. For low-volume office materials, dedicated hardware and integration often cost more than the administrative savings.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing forms, validation, and formulas can remove lookup and calculation effort with little custom work. No new capability is assumed for physical handling.
tasks.still_hard: Mixed items, packaging, damaged materials, inaccurate instruments, and awkward storage require physical inspection.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise items that look similar, handle fragile materials, and investigate mismatches at the shelf.
tasks.altitude: Physical handling still fills most of this task. The clerk can spend saved recording time identifying shortages; purchasing authority stays unchanged.

reach.task: Prepare a discrepancy list for incoming office supplies.
reach.learn: Use consistent units, location codes, and receipt reconciliation.

evidence.claim: Validated records and formulas can reduce recording and calculation work but do not automate physical counting or handling.
The proposed scope and effort estimates assume low-volume materials and no new measurement hardware.

assumptions: This instance concerns low-volume office supplies, print materials, and cartons.
A shared {SPREADSHEET} is the current register; an existing {OPS_SYSTEM} should be configured instead where available.
Time shares put most effort in physical work, exceeding the prior's physical-means estimate.
No automated weighing, machine vision, or robotics is included.
Records contain material data rather than employee productivity measures. GDPR, EU AI Act requirements, and national rules apply where relevant.
unknowns: Material volumes, variability, and required measurement accuracy.
Whether an existing {OPS_SYSTEM} already supports this process.
Available storage codes, access permissions, and consultation requirements.
research_questions: Does validated entry reduce recording time without increasing unit or location errors?
Is an existing stock-management function cheaper to configure than the shared register?
new_work: Maintain item codes, units, and storage locations.
Investigate validation exceptions and correct source records.
Check formulas and permissions when the register changes.

tasks.short: Diagnose routine office-equipment problems, attempt approved fixes, and escalate unresolved faults.

steps.what: Collect symptoms and device details through the {EMAIL}.
Inspect the equipment and reproduce the reported problem.
Find relevant troubleshooting instructions in the {DOCS}.
Apply routine fixes within the clerk's authorised support scope.
Send unresolved faults and attempted fixes to the IT support team through the {EMAIL}.
Confirm the equipment works during normal use.

tasks.design: Configure a structured intake form and device-specific troubleshooting paths in the {HELPDESK}, linked to approved guides in the {DOCS}. The clerk performs authorised fixes, while recorded symptoms and attempts automatically populate internal escalations and closure requests.
tasks.previous_blocker: Symptoms arrived incompletely, guides were scattered, and escalation required repeating the same details. Physical diagnosis remained difficult to standardise.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing helpdesk forms, knowledge search, and routing rules can cover this narrow scope. Faster configuration and small integrations lower setup effort without requiring autonomous diagnosis.
tasks.still_hard: Intermittent faults, unfamiliar equipment, physical repairs, and permission-dependent changes still need skilled support.
tasks.human_edge: Observe the actual failure, recognise when a routine fix is inappropriate, and verify that normal work can resume.
tasks.altitude: The clerk spends less time finding instructions and rewriting escalations, and more time spotting repeat faults. Repair, software-installation, and access rights remain unchanged.

reach.task: Prepare equipment-replacement recommendations from recurring faults.
reach.learn: Use aggregate fault frequency, downtime, warranty status, and replacement cost.

evidence.claim: Structured intake, knowledge search, decision paths, and internal escalation commonly fit configured helpdesk functions.
Physical diagnosis and repair remain human in this design; a model loop is unnecessary for a bounded catalogue of approved fixes.

assumptions: The clerk provides first-line assistance rather than specialist IT administration.
An existing {HELPDESK} supports forms, knowledge articles, and routing.
The employee supplies structured symptoms; this creates a small intake burden outside the clerk's saved time.
Escalation occurs only for unresolved faults, so its share is averaged across cases.
Estimates cover common office devices and approved fixes.
GDPR applies to incident data; EU AI Act requirements and consultation under national rules are assessed as applicable.
unknowns: The clerk's authorised fixes and escalation thresholds.
Available device records, knowledge articles, and helpdesk configuration rights.
The proportion of faults requiring specialist or external support.
Whether diagnostic data includes personal information or employee monitoring.
research_questions: Can existing helpdesk configuration cover the most common faults without generated advice?
Does structured escalation reduce follow-up questions and repeat visits?
new_work: Maintain approved troubleshooting paths and device mappings.
Review misrouted incidents and incomplete intake forms.
Remove obsolete fixes and track recurring equipment faults.

role.altitude: The office clerk keeps the physical, teaching, and situational parts of the job while routine preparation and coordination shrink. Saved time supports clearer meeting follow-through, targeted coaching, and earlier identification of office problems; formal approval and spending rights require explicit delegation.
reach: Project management specialist: prepare action-dependency reviews.
Administrative services manager: recommend training priorities and equipment replacements.
Shipping, receiving, and inventory clerk: reconcile incoming office-material discrepancies.
skills_to_grow: Configure forms, templates, validation, and approval flows.
Check generated text against source notes and approved procedures.
Teach practical application skills and accommodate different learning needs.
Use consistent material, device, and incident records.
Interpret aggregate service patterns and make supported recommendations.
Apply access, retention, and consultation requirements to office workflows.
role.ambitious_version: Provide a weekly office-readiness review covering unresolved meeting decisions, recurring equipment faults, material shortages, and training needs, with named recommendations for the responsible managers.
